long_biography.plain_text:
Nidal Ghazi Karameh, who conducts business publicly as Mofid Karameh, is a Nigerian industrialist with a mechanical-engineering background. In a Forbes Africa interview, he said he graduated in 1988, moved to Nigeria in 1990 and established Mikano in 1993. The company began with generator importing, servicing and maintenance before pioneering local assembly, turning Nigeria's unreliable power supply into the foundation for a manufacturing business.

Karameh remains Mikano International's chairman and chief executive. The group now covers power generation, steel fabrication, electrical systems, heavy equipment, automotive assembly, construction, food, medical manufacturing and marine products. UK corporate records independently identify Nidal Ghazi Karameh, born in June 1965, as a Nigerian-resident managing director within the Mikano network and give him director-appointment rights. The breadth of the operating group supports a diversified, self-made founder classification, though public records do not disclose a consolidated ownership map or segment values.

The dossier treats Mofid as the public business name but keeps identity confidence at high rather than very high.

No exact Forbes profile was found for Nidal Ghazi, Nidal Chazi or Mofid Karameh. The 2022 Forbes Africa interview is a direct feature, not a Forbes profile, so the Forbes-profile status remains not_found.

Mikano's operating portfolio is clearly multi-sector, but consolidated ownership, financial accounts and segment values are not public. Diversified reflects the documented breadth of the founder-led group rather than a quantified personal net-worth allocation.

Companies House shows that Omar Nidal Karameh owns at least 75 percent of the small UK affiliate, while Nidal retains director-appointment rights. That affiliate structure was not extrapolated to the Nigerian parent or the wider group.

The precise birthplace was not established at the required confidence and is not proposed. The source record's Syrian birth country and Syrian secondary nationality were preserved but not used to infer a city.
